THE FIX ROUND'S ONE FINDING, AND WHY THE RESULT IS UNCHANGED

The fix file `/Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets/.dev/inprocess/114-kit-page-narration/fixes-for-the-identity-test.md` carries exactly one finding: the identity spelling the tests pin "is a format other people write their narration beats against, and the contract carried it on the orchestrator's word rather than Tim's." Its instruction is "Nothing to the tests ... Re-return the same result," and it orders me to check both the tests and the contract myself rather than take its word.

I did. The finding no longer stands, and I verified that against the contract's own words rather than the fix file's. The contract now carries decision `identity-spelling` at `.dev/inprocess/114-kit-page-narration/contract.md:37`: "The number in a repeated member's identity counts only the rows carrying that same name, starting at one, so two members of one declaration both named `PrecheckAsync` are `PrecheckAsync#1` and `PrecheckAsync#2` however many other members the declaration holds, and adding an unrelated member above them changes neither. Tim approved this as written on 2026-11-13, answering `identity-spelling` with `among-the-shared` in pkg-f1d7e85abb9f. ... A member whose name is not repeated keeps its plain name, unchanged."

WHAT THE TESTS PIN, CHECKED LINE BY LINE AGAINST THAT DECISION

The three cases sit in `ts/metalang/app.test.tsx:1888-1953`, under `describe('two members of one declaration carrying one name')`, and every clause of the decision has a case:

- Counting among the shared rows, from one. The fixture `overloaded()` at :1902-1910 declares `Name`, then `PrecheckAsync`, then `PrecheckAsync`. The test at :1923-1930 requires `PrecheckAsync#1` and `PrecheckAsync#2`. Had the number counted among all of the declaration's members they would be `#2` and `#3`, so the unrelated `Name` above them is what makes the fixture discriminate between the spelling Tim approved and the one he refused. This is the clause the lie-catcher flagged, and it is now his.
- The bare shared name on no row. :1933-1936 requires `[data-member="PrecheckAsync"]` to match nothing.
- A name that is not repeated keeps its plain name. :1938-1952 draws a declaration naming each member once and requires `Name` and `PrecheckAsync` to each reach their one row, with `[data-member*="#"]` matching nothing anywhere on the page.

Nothing in the tests exceeds or falls short of the decision, so there was nothing to report back instead of a result.

WHAT I CHANGED: NOTHING

No file is edited. `git status` is clean and the three cases stand exactly as commit a01f52d wrote them (`73\t0` on `ts/metalang/app.test.tsx` — 73 insertions, no deletions, so no existing assertion was touched). I did not commit and did not push.
